title: Adaptive Chokepoint Autotuner for Dedicated Fleets
creator: Daniel Kim
description:
Goal: Build an autoscaling policy component that tunes per-fleet scaling decisions around identified chokepoints (e.g., kernel saturation, KV-cache miss spikes, IO stalls) while enforcing per-tenant throughput guarantees and safety limits. The component — the 'Chokepoint Autotuner' — will synthesize target metrics (percentile latency, tokens/s, cache-hit-rate), select a scaling algorithm per situation (constrained PID loop, quantized stepper, or solver-backed min-cost allocation), and apply a tiered rollback/shed strategy when safety envelopes are breached.

Scope: prototype runtime hook + policy DSL + operator controls in Console. Not responsible for allocator implementation; will expose scale intents and fenced commit requests to the existing orchestrator.

Design highlights: 1) Multi-signal targets: primary target is 95th percentile per-request latency and tokens/s per-GPU; secondary targets include KV cache hit-rate and GPU core utilization. 2) Multi-horizon control: immediate micro-adjustments (5s–30s) via a constrained PID with anti-windup; medium horizon (1–10m) uses a solver to reassign committed slots based on tenant contracts; long horizon (10m–1h) adapts quantization of commit sizes and headroom budgets. 3) Safety envelope: define soft and hard boundaries: soft triggers produce conservative step-up/step-down; hard triggers halt scale-up and initiate graceful degradation/traffic shedding to configured tiers. 4) Rollback tiers: incremental rollout, canary gating, automatic rollback on regression (quality or latency), and an operator-visible 'revert-to-stable' action. 5) Telemetry + tracing: per-decision debug traces, token-level cost deltas, and a 'why-did-we-scale' event that surfaces the dominant signal and constraint.

APIs & Ops: CLI/Console controls to set per-fleet: throughput-contracts, min/max commit quanta, burst budgets, safety thresholds, and allowed scaling algorithms. Policy runs in the control plane but with a light-weight decision agent co-located with fleet leaders for low-latency enforcement.

Why this is different: Most existing controllers either optimize a single metric or apply uniform elasticity rules. The autotuner explicitly reasons about chokepoints, composes heterogeneous metrics, and enforces contractual guarantees via a constrained decision layer rather than blind scaling heuristics.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype can ingest runtime signals (p95 latency, tokens/s, cache-hit-rate, GPU util) and emit scale-intents to the orchestrator
Decision traces recorded and viewable in Console for at least 24h of test traffic
Respect per-fleet min/max commit quanta and do not exceed hard safety thresholds in chaos tests
Automatic rollback triggers on 10% regression in p95 or 5% quality drift as measured by evaluation harness
End-to-end test with 3 tenants showing throughput guarantees honored under burst + sustained load
test_plan: Unit tests for PID and solver components with synthetic signal inputs
Integration test in staging: replay production traces with injected KV-cache miss storms
Chaos experiment: throttle model kernel to simulate chokepoint and assert autoscaler enters safe-shed state
Canary rollout to a single small Dedicated fleet with manual operator monitoring
Load test with mixed tenants to validate per-tenant contract enforcement
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: overfitting to synthetic traces causing oscillation. Mitigation: add hysteresis and quantized commits; use historical smoothing windows.
Risk: decision latency adds to control loop. Mitigation: colocate a lightweight agent for enforcement and only run expensive solver periodically.
Risk: rollback causes customer-visible throttling. Mitigation: tiered shedding with customer-priority mapping and pre-announced fallback routes.
Risk: metric noise (p95 spikes) causing unnecessary scaling. Mitigation: require multi-signal agreement and minimum sustained window before commit.
rollout_plan: Week 1: unit/prototype iteration in dev cluster and design review (Confluence draft)
Week 2: integration with orchestrator + visibility hooks; internal demo
Week 3: staged canary to one Dedicated fleet; run synthetic burst tests
Week 4: expand to 3 fleets and enable automatic rollback triggers; monitor for 7d before broad rollout
